newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Habibie says nuclear power last option.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Habibie says nuclear power last option.

text.p: Nuclear power was Indonesia's last option, Indonesian Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie said on Wednesday.
"Nuclear power is the last option," Habibie told reporters, adding that if Indonesia could do without nuclear power then it would.

Last week Habibie said a study which determined that Indonesia needed a nuclear power station by 2003 was conducted 20 years ago before a number of key oil and gas reserves as well as other energy sources were discovered.

"Maybe, we will finally need a nuclear power station in 2020 or 2030. Now we have an excess supply of electricity. Because of that our energy needs need to be revised again," he told a Jakarta conference last week.
Habibie said the revisions were necessary because of the discovery of natural gas reserves in Natuna, Irian Jaya and Kalimantan as well as the use of geothermal energy.
Last month, Indonesia's parliament passed a controversial nuclear energy bill which anti-nuclear activists said was designed to pave the way for building Indonesia's first nuclear power station.

Agencies under Habibie's control had previously said they planned to start building a 7,200 megawatt nuclear power station with foreign help at Mount Muria in central Java in 1998 or 1999 pending the results of a feasiblity study.
Indonesia has extensive reserves of oil, natural gas and coal, but little uranium.
